learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of the principles of machine and mechanism theory.
Knowledge and capabilities for the calculation, design, and testing of machines.
Knows and applies the principles of machine analysis and calculation.
Knows how to apply failure criteria for mechanical dimensioning.
Establishes models for the analysis of machine elements.
Calculates, dimensions, and selects machine elements for an application.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.

assessment_methods.method: Written exam - Problems Part I (course content)
Written exam - Problems Part II (continuous assessment and practicals)

assessment_rules: The final grade will be the maximum of two paths: (Theoretical-practical questions + Problems Part I + Problems Part II) or (Theoretical-practical questions + Problems Part I + Continuous Assessment Activities). In both cases, the final grade must be 5 points or higher to pass the course. Students may be required to demonstrate authorship of assignments/practicals in an oral interview; otherwise, those assignments will receive a 0.
